en: a. very serious or bad; strict or harsh; (of a style) very plain and without decoration
ex: The storm caused severe damage to the coastal towns.
暴風雨對沿海城鎮造成嚴重的破壞。

en: a. following traditional methods or accepted ways of doing things; (of weapons or energy) not nuclear; ordinary and not unusual
ex: They had a conventional wedding in a church.
他們在教堂舉行了傳統的婚禮。

en: n. an amount of money that you borrow from a bank and must pay back; the act of lending something; v. to lend something, especially money, to someone
ex: He took out a loan to buy a house.
他貸款買了一棟房子。

en: n. a person who does something for pleasure and not as a job; a person who lacks skill or experience; a. done for pleasure and not as a job
ex: He is an amateur photographer who sells some of his work.
他是業餘攝影師，也會賣掉一些作品。

en: n. a small device worn over or in the ear for listening to music or sound; the part of a telephone you hold to your ear
ex: He listened to music with his earphones on the train.
他在火車上戴著耳機聽音樂。

en: n. the state of being without protection from something harmful; the act of making something known; the amount of light that reaches a camera film or sensor
ex: Too much exposure to the sun can damage your skin.
過度曝曬在陽光下會傷害皮膚。

en: a. always behaving or happening in the same way; agreeing with something else; not containing parts that disagree with each other
ex: Her grades have been consistent all semester.
她整個學期的成績都很穩定。

en: n. a doctor who performs surgical operations; a doctor in the army or navy
ex: The surgeon performed a successful heart operation.
外科醫生成功完成了一場心臟手術。

en: n. the system of money, trade and industry in a country; the careful use of money or resources; the state of a country's finances; a. cheap and economical
ex: The country's economy grew by three percent last year.
該國經濟去年成長了百分之三。

en: a. relating to philosophy; calm and accepting when something bad happens; showing wisdom in the way you deal with difficulties
ex: He was philosophical about losing the game.
他對輸掉比賽看得很開。

en: vi. to close and open one eye quickly as a signal; (of a light) to shine and go out quickly; vt. to close and open one eye quickly; n. a quick closing and opening of one eye; a very short time
ex: He winked at me across the room.
他隔著房間朝我眨了眨眼。

en: n. the quality of being important; the meaning of something; the special meaning that something has
ex: We must not underestimate the significance of this discovery.
我們不能低估這項發現的重要性。

en: n. a person who acts for another person or organization in business; a secret officer who collects information; a substance that causes a chemical change
ex: She works as a real estate agent in the city.
她在市區做房地產經紀人。

en: n. the cost of sending a letter or parcel by mail
ex: The price includes postage and packing.
價格包含郵資與包裝費。

en: n. a new thing that someone has made for the first time; the act of making something new; something that is made up and not true
ex: The invention of the telephone changed the world.
電話的發明改變了世界。
ph: necessity is the mother of invention

en: n. an object or structure built to remind people of an event or a person who has died; a statement to a government asking for something; a. built or done to remember someone or something
ex: A memorial was built to honor the soldiers who died in the war.
為紀念戰爭中陣亡的士兵，人們建了一座紀念碑。

en: n. the feeling that you can trust someone or something; belief in your own abilities; a secret that you tell someone and trust them not to tell others
ex: She spoke with great confidence in front of the audience.
她在觀眾面前非常有自信地說話。

en: n. a system that uses radio waves to find the position and speed of objects such as aircraft and ships; the device that does this
ex: The radar showed an aircraft approaching from the north.
雷達顯示有一架飛機從北方接近。

en: n. a curved structure that supports a bridge or a roof; a curved shape; the curved part of the bottom of your foot; vt. to curve something into a bow shape; vi. to form a curve
ex: The old stone bridge has three arches.
那座古老的石橋有三個拱門。

en: vt. to suggest something indirectly without saying it directly; to have something as a necessary result
ex: His silence seemed to imply that he disagreed.
他的沉默似乎暗示他不同意。

en: n. the act of moving someone or something from one place to another; a change from one job, school or team to another; a ticket that lets you change from one vehicle to another; vt. to move something from one place to another; vi. to change to another place
ex: He asked for a transfer to the Tokyo office.
他申請調到東京辦事處。

en: n. a strong, cool cloth made from the flax plant, used for clothes and household items; sheets, tablecloths, towels and other cloth items used in the house; a. made of linen
ex: She wore a light linen dress in the summer.
她夏天穿著一件輕薄的亞麻洋裝。

en: n. a medicine or treatment that cures a disease or illness; a way to solve a problem; legal compensation for a wrong; vt. to correct something that is wrong; to cure an illness
ex: Rest is the best remedy for a cold.
休息是治療感冒最好的辦法。

en: a. considered to be socially acceptable or morally good; of a fairly large size or amount; fairly good; n. a person who is socially acceptable
ex: He earns a respectable salary as an engineer.
他當工程師，薪水相當不錯。

en: n. the act of stopping someone from doing something for a short time; a break in the continuity of something; something that stops a process
ex: I'm sorry for the interruption, but you have a phone call.
抱歉打擾一下，你有一通電話。

en: a. relating to art or artists; showing skill and imagination in making or arranging things; good at drawing, painting or music
ex: She comes from an artistic family and plays the violin.
她來自一個藝術世家，會拉小提琴。

en: n. a room or building with equipment for doing scientific experiments or tests; a place where chemicals or medicines are made
ex: The students did an experiment in the chemistry laboratory.
學生們在化學實驗室做了一個實驗。

en: vi. to try very hard to achieve something; to fight against something or someone
ex: We strive to provide the best service to our customers.
我們努力為顧客提供最好的服務。

en: n. a vegetable such as a cucumber preserved in vinegar or salty water; liquid used for preserving food; a difficult or unpleasant situation; vt. to preserve food in vinegar or salty water
ex: She added pickles to the sandwich.
她在三明治裡加了醃黃瓜。

en: a. needing to be dealt with immediately; asking for something with a lot of force or energy
ex: I received an urgent message from the hospital.
我收到了醫院的緊急訊息。

en: a. very sad because it involves death or suffering; relating to tragedy in literature; causing great sadness
ex: The tragic accident took the lives of three young people.
那起悲慘的意外奪走了三個年輕人的性命。

en: n. a great success or victory; a feeling of great happiness after winning; vi. to win a victory; to achieve success
ex: The team's triumph was celebrated all across the city.
球隊的勝利在全市受到慶祝。

en: n. a curved piece of metal or plastic used for hanging or catching things; a way of attracting attention; a punch in boxing; vt. to catch something with a hook; to attach something with a hook; vi. to be fastened by a hook
ex: Hang your coat on the hook behind the door.
把你的外套掛在門後面的鉤子上。

en: n. a person who cannot stop taking drugs or doing something harmful; a person who is very interested in something; vt. to make someone depend on something harmful
ex: He became a coffee addict and drinks six cups a day.
他成了咖啡成癮者，一天喝六杯。

en: n. a clear difference between two things; a thing that is very different from something else; vt. to show the differences between two things; vi. to be clearly different from something
ex: There is a sharp contrast between the rich and the poor.
貧富之間有鮮明的對比。

en: n. the health and happiness of a person or group; financial aid given by a government to people who need it; a. relating to such aid
ex: The government has increased spending on social welfare.
政府增加了社會福利的支出。

en: a. felt or done by both people or groups; shared by two or more people; belonging to two or more people
ex: The feeling of respect between them is mutual.
他們之間的尊敬是相互的。

en: n. a red color on the face caused by strong emotion or heat; a sudden flow of water; a sudden strong feeling; a. level with another surface; vt. to clean something with a rush of water; vi. (of a face) to become red
ex: Her face flushed with embarrassment.
她因為尷尬而臉紅了。

en: a. relating to the sun; using energy from the sun; (of a calendar) based on the position of the sun
ex: The house is heated by solar energy.
這間房子是用太陽能供暖的。

en: n. a person who gives their opinion about the good and bad qualities of books, films, music or art; a person who finds fault with someone or something
ex: The film critic gave the movie four stars.
影評人給這部電影四顆星。
